hook_text: With your eyes, it's just a bright dot. Through a telescope, it has stripes and four moons!
clip_script: Stargazing night in Soweto. Field lights off. That bright dot? Jupiter. Now look through the telescope: stripes and four tiny moons! How? A telescope is a light bucket. Its mirror is way wider than your pupil, so it catches way more light. Lenses bend light, mirrors bounce it. Radio dishes catch waves we can't see. And never, ever point it at the Sun!
visual_style: Whiteboard eye next to a wide telescope mirror catching many more light rays, then Jupiter with four moons.
mood: Hushed night-time excitement with a big reveal.
pacing: Slow build to the look through the eyepiece, then quick facts.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find Jupiter or the Moon on the next clear night.
